identity: A page from the Emirati children's comic magazine Majid. Tokens 0-28 are the cover / contents block: the masthead ماجد, then five illustrated teaser lines (كسلان جدا يبحث عن اسم لجواده / دانة ترتدي أجمل ثيابها لحضور حفل مهم / مركبة فضاء يقودها قرد / درهم أنا لست بخيلا / آخر العنقود). Tokens 30-154 are the آخر العنقود comic strip itself: a Beautiful Child contest with a free cup of milk, the spoiled boy setting the other children against each other, the judge refusing to award the prize, and the closing gag that all he won was an old bucket. There is no narration and no speech verb anywhere - the entire body is balloon text, caption boxes (فيما بعد) and sound effects (هاها, هه). Register: children's comic. The natural unit is the balloon line, roughly 3-4 content tokens, not the paragraph.
law: Layout is the sentence here. Every <NL> is a hard boundary and the final token is a boundary: that is 27 of my 36 segments, free. Inside a line I reconstruct the ink, not the meaning, and I cut only where the printed page must have carried a mark: (1) a label or name followed by material that cannot be its predicate - a character name plus a first-person title, a poster headline plus its offer line, a complete clause plus the bare appositive name that answers it; (2) two complete clauses juxtaposed asyndetically where the second cannot attach syntactically to the first; (3) a free-standing interjection that governs nothing. I do NOT cut between a subject and its own verb in a headline teaser; I do NOT split an interjection or discourse adverbial from the vocative, imperative or clause it governs; I do NOT strip a trailing purpose or causal clause off its main clause (LAW 4); and in this register I do NOT pull a و-clause out of reported speech even when it brings a new argument, because §F3 - same magazine register, same configuration - shows the gold welding it.
reasoning: Register first (LAW 6): comic-balloon text, so the target unit is one balloon line and 27 boundaries come free from <NL> plus the final token. That leaves nine internal sites to argue. (a) Teasers. 2-7 كسلان جدا يبحث عن اسم لجواده and 9-15 دانة ترتدي أجمل ثيابها لحضور حفل مهم are well-formed single clauses (topic + its own verb), so I did NOT cut after جدا@3 or دانة@9, even though Arabic magazine covers often set a character name off with an ellipsis - the gold reconstructs ink, and no ink is required between a subject and its verb. But 22-25 درهم أنا لست بخيلا cannot be one clause: درهم is a bare NP and أنا لست بخيلا is a complete nominal sentence, so a colon or ellipsis is forced. CUT @22, hi. That is the §A4 title-colon shape and the §K3 caption shape, and it is why I do not need to make the other two teasers exceptions. (b) 30-37 مسابقة الطفل الجميل كوب حليب مجانا لكل الأطفال is a contest poster: headline NP then offer NP, two NPs that cannot form one clause without a separator. CUT @32, hi (§J2 page furniture, §K3 caption subject splits from predicate). (c) 41-48 انظروا من سيشارك في المسابقة معنا آخر العنقود: a complete imperative clause followed by the bare name that answers it. §G2 says apposition cuts even inside speech, and LAW 3 files apposition with repetition. CUT @46, hi. (d) Asyndetic double clauses, four of them, all the same verdict: 50-59 ربما كان أصدقائي على حق || كل هؤلاء الأطفال أجمل مني (CUT @54) - كل هؤلاء الأطفال cannot continue على حق; 75-79 هو قال ذلك || سأجعله يرى (CUT @77); 116-121 جعلتهم كلهم يتشاجرون || أكيد سأفوز أنا (CUT @118); 126-134 يا إلهي || لا أستطيع منح الجائزة لأي من هؤلاء (CUT @127), where يا إلهي is a complete exclamatory utterance and not a vocative bound to what follows. All hi: in each case the second unit is syntactically unattachable to the first, so the source had a full stop or an exclamation. (e) The hardest site is @70, مدلل | ويكفيك مداعبة دميتك, inside بست هذا يقول إنك لن تفوز لأنك مدلل ويكفيك مداعبة دميتك. LAW 1 argues CUT: ويكفيك has its own predicate and its own new subject مداعبة دميتك, and LAW 1 accounted for about 120 of my 231 batch-1 misses. Against it stands §F3, the closest precedent I own - same register (children's magazine), same configuration (quoted speech plus و plus a new-argument clause) - and there the gold WELDED (لتعمل في بيتي الجديد خادما وسوف أجعل زوجي يقدم لك أفضل أنواع الطعام). §G1 agrees: a reported utterance rides with its speech verb, and here everything after يقول إن is one report, with ويكفيك still inside the scope of لأنك. A register-matched precedent beats a general law, so NO CUT @70. I did cut the opening interjection: بست is psst, an attention-getter governing nothing, and §H3 says a bare interjection carried its own mark. CUT @63, med. The document backs this - هاها, وجدتها and فرصة each occupy a whole line, so this page isolates exclamations by habit. (f) 106-109 شربت مني اللبن هه: هه is an unbound trailing sneer, syntactically governing nothing, and by the same habit it is its own unit. This is a genuine coin flip and LAW 0 says cut at coin flips. CUT @108, lo. (g) Three declines, all on one principle - an interjection or adverbial that GOVERNS what follows stays with it. يو هو أمي @88: أمي is the addressee of the call, and the in-document parallel مرحبا أمي (93-94) is certainly a single greeting, so both are treated the same. حسنا خذ المزيد منه @111: the LAW 4 mirror says short discourse adverbials attach forward to the clause they modify. هيا بنا لنرى إن كان والدك يستطيع تخليصك @137: the ل-clause is the purpose of هيا بنا, and LAW 4 keeps a trailing subordinate with its main clause. (h) Density check against LAW 0. 36 boundaries over 129 content tokens is 3.6 tokens per segment, and my longest surviving segment is the 10-token بست balloon. Batch 1 failed by leaving 20-token runs standing; none survive here, so I am not repeating that failure even though I declined four internal cuts.
